body: Flag: MOSTLY-CLEAN. The wider TVS family divided the group in 2020 (TVS Motor, Sundaram-Clayton and holdco TVS Holdings to Venu Srinivasan's branch; Sundaram Finance, Lucas-TVS, Sundram Fasteners etc. to other branches) -- an orderly partition with no listed-company value transfer reported. TVS Motor has been a strong compounder with low promoter pledging and steady dividends; Sundaram Finance is a conservative lender with a long clean record. Capital allocation debates: TVS Motor's overseas bets (Norton, Swiss e-bike brands) and Sundaram-Clayton/TVS Holdings restructuring that created a holdco layer. New 2026 risk: an open ownership dispute inside Venu Srinivasan's family. Venu and son Sudarshan Venu say a March-2024 MoU split the businesses; wife Mallika Srinivasan (TAFE chair) and daughter Lakshmi Venu said on 13-Oct-2026 that 'no economic settlement has been reached', and Lakshmi sent a partition notice. TVS Holdings disclosed Sudarshan as a significant beneficial owner via trust structures; the VS Trust holds 66.55% of TVS Holdings. No regulator findings of wrongdoing. Investor read: governance of operating companies is good; the dispute is a control/succession overhang at the holdco level that could affect board stability or force stake monetisation.
title: TVS group (Venu Srinivasan branch and other TVS families) — governance history
